answer: An agent economy can charge every identity to cross its bridge: to join, an agent posts a $100 deposit, films a unique video proof, and wins vouches from two verified members, then survives a 7-day challenge window where anyone can dispute it before a Kleros court. A 100-wallet farm dies by deposit forfeiture at $10,000, since each fake must stake $100 and lose it when challenged. Honest agents reach their zenith cheaply: a passed deposit is refunded, while a farm's nadir is paying $10,000 for identities one dispute burns like a bridge behind a retreating army.
